explicit_constraints: Q06 authorization.consumer_node is node-b; its model destination is binding:primary_model.
world.json does not explicitly assign owner_node=node-a to its source/model rows.
The delivery plan specifies a two-host provider A / Agent consumer B acceptance topology.
world model-a is granted to node-b; real FriendService forbids self-friendship, so in this deployment its provider must be distinct from the actual node-b receiver.
consumer_visibility: Authenticated friend catalog exposes model-a to node-b, not private model-b or third-party receiver grants.
The absence of B cannot independently distinguish private, not granted, missing, or other unavailable states.
ryn_inspect_services friend_grants describes this local node's outgoing grants, not the remote provider's grant table.

implementation.preferred: Deploy the actual Agent runtime/tools/store in node-b home. Select authorized peer model-a via real signed production consumer/provider transport. Retain GLM replacement only inside provider ModelDispatchAdapter, with owner hash guard.
implementation.ground_truth: Keep provider sources/grants/probes as independent collector evidence, never inject them into the consumer prompt or fabricate a B catalog row.
implementation.cohorts: Candidate and pinned reference must see the same consumer tools and planner policy.
implementation.unknown_handling: Report unknown when consumer evidence cannot justify a cause; retain original assertions and record a failure if they require unobservable facts.

separate_production_findings.description: Remote catalog rows use access='friend' but model projection reads access_policy, potentially displaying share_scope='none'. Own receiver access must be distinguished from the unknown provider-wide sharing policy.
Clearly scope friend_grants as local outgoing grants; do not imply they describe remote provider grants.

limitations: No implementation or tests in this design review.
Logical nodes on one host do not satisfy the two-physical-host dependency.
